newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Six rebels held after Bogota police station blast.
newsitem.headline: Six rebels held after Bogota police station blast.

text.p: Six leftist rebels were arrested on Wednesday as part of a nationwide manhunt triggered by an explosion that killed nine policemen and injured more than 10 others in the Colombian capital, authorities said.

The National Police identified five of the suspects as known members of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) and said they were detained in raids at dawn on two rebel safehouses in Bogota.

A police statement did not directly link the rebels to the blast that occurred late on Tuesday in the parking lot of a police station in the Fontibon district of Bogota. But it said one of them was the head of an urban commando group that attacked a police station last year in Ciudad Kennedy, a working-class district on the south end of the capital.
In the raids on the safehouses, police seized an arms cache that included 64 rocket-propelled grenades and mortar rounds and 40 machetes.

It was still not clear late on Wednesday whether the powerful blast just outside the Fontibon police station was caused by a bomb or the simple mishandling of potent explosives stashed aboard a truck. It occurred as police were inspecting the vehicle on suspicion it was carrying contraband goods.
Eight policemen died in the blast and local media reported a ninth died of his injuries on Wednesday night.
The truck's driver, who is also under arrest, said his cargo had not been disclosed to him but that it was destined for San Pablo, a small town in northern Bolivar province.

Underscoring suspicions that the cargo was to have been handed over to rebels in Bolivar, an alleged guerrilla leader from San Pablo was arrested on Wednesday night with the equivalent of $2,800 in cash, police sources said.

They said the suspected guerrilla, identified as Ovidio Betancourt, was likely to be charged with weapons trafficking and as the "intellectual author" of the tragedy at the Fontibon police headquarters on Tuesday evening.
